sheets.noticed: A blueprint-style grid with 'PEDAL' and 'WHEEL' labels. It looks like a technical diagram, so I'm curious but not hooked yet.
'The brake pedal' gets labeled, then '5 CM' appears next to the pedal. The small number gives me a reason to stay.
'So how does that stop a' asks a question over the same diagram. The question keeps me watching.
'TWO TONS' appears beside the wheel. Now the contrast with the 5 cm pedal makes me want the answer.
A piston and 'PUSH' arrows animate into the pedal. The motion helps, I'm still in.
'A cylinder full of brake fluid' with brake fluid labels stacking. Busy but it's building.
'Can't be squeezed' appears over the brake fluid. A clean idea, so I keep going.
'So the pressure travels' with the lines now labeled. Still following the chain.
'Brake line' and 'pressure' labels add to the stack. Getting dense, but it's still moving.
'Caliper' lights up at the bottom of the stack, then 'at the wheel'. The chain finally reaches the wheel.
The diagram freezes with the same labels for two seconds, 'that pressure pushes' is said over nothing new. I swipe away here.

remembers: Pushing the brake pedal a few centimeters pushes a piston into brake fluid, which can't be squeezed, so the pressure travels to each wheel. I only heard up to the caliper before swiping.
